questions.question: Explain the role of creative writing in media industry / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Creative writing in the media industry helps produce engaging, original, and impactful
  • content across platforms like advertising, television, digital media, journalism, and film. It
  • enhances storytelling, captures audience interest, builds emotional connection, and adds
  • artistic value to factual or promotional messages. Creative writing also strengthens brand
  • identity, improves message recall, and allows media professionals to communicate complex
  • ideas in accessible and imaginative ways. [U] / [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is literal translation and when is it used in journalism? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Literal translation is a word-for-word rendering of a source text, preserving original structure
  • and vocabulary as closely as possible. In journalism, it is used when accuracy and neutrality
  • are crucial—such as translating official statements, legal documents, speeches, data, and
  • direct quotes—where altering wording may change meaning or cause misinterpretation.
  • [U] / [CO3]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is “engagement” in social media writing? / [CO4, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Engagement refers to the level of interaction users have with social media content. It includes
  • likes, comments, shares, saves, clicks, reactions, and time spent viewing. High engagement
  • indicates that the content is relevant, relatable, and effective in prompting user participation,
  • discussions, or community building. [An] / [CO4, CO5]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain significance of translation in global news organizations / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Translation enables global news organizations to gather, distribute, and share information
  • across linguistic boundaries. It ensures fast dissemination of worldwide events, helps
  • maintain accuracy while reporting international stories, and allows news agencies to reach
  • diverse audiences. Translation supports cross-cultural understanding, reduces
  • misinformation, and strengthens global connectivity in journalism. [U] / [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss intersemiotic translation with examples / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Intersemiotic translation (Roman Jakobson) refers to translating meaning from one sign
  • system to another—not between languages, but between different modes such as text, image,
  • sound, or film.
  • Examples: A novel adapted into a film, A poem turned into a painting or music, A news
  • report converted into an infographic, A historical event represented as a documentary.
  • [U] / [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is creative writing / [CO4, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Creative writing is a form of expressive writing that uses imagination, narrative craft, and
  • artistic techniques to convey ideas, emotions, and stories. It includes genres such as fiction,
  • poetry, drama, scripts, and personal essays. It emphasizes originality, figurative language,
  • character development, and engaging storytelling. [U] / [CO4, CO5]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain processes of gate keeping and transediting in journalistic translation / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Gatekeeping:
  • The selection, filtering, and control of news content by editors or journalists. In translation,
  • gatekeeping decides which foreign stories are chosen, what information is included or
  • excluded, and how content aligns with editorial policies.
  • Trans editing:
  • A blend of translation, editing, and rewriting. Journalists modify the original text to suit space
  • limits, cultural expectations, style guidelines, or clarity requirements. It may involve
  • summarizing, reorganizing, simplifying, or adapting content to fit the target audience and
  • medium. [U] / [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does audience diversity influence translation choices in journalism? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Audience diversity influences translators to adapt language, tone, cultural references, and
  • examples to ensure comprehension across varied demographic, linguistic, and cultural
  • groups. They may avoid idioms, simplify complex terms, provide context, and maintain
  • neutral or inclusive language to cater to multicultural and multilingual audiences. [K] / [CO3]

questions.question: Explain advantages of computer assisted translation / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• CAT tools assist human translators using technology such as translation memory,
  • terminology databases, and alignment tools. Advantages include: Faster translation with
  • increased efficiency- Consistency in terminology and phrasing-Reduced errors- Reuse of
  • previous translations-better collaboration among translators-Ability to handle large projects
  • systematically. [U] / [CO1]

questions.question: How do cultural references affect subtitle translation? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Cultural references may not have direct equivalents in the target language, making subtitle
  • translation challenging. Translators must adapt, simplify, or replace references with culturally
  • understandable alternatives while preserving meaning. Misalignment can cause confusion or
  • loss of humour, emotion, or context. Space and time constraints in subtitles make this
  • adaptation even more crucial. [U] / [CO3]

questions.solution_html:
• Personal voice in column writing adds individuality, perspective, and emotion to a writer’s
  • opinion. It differentiates the columnist’s style, builds reader trust, and creates a recognizable
  • persona. Personal voice allows use of humor, anecdotes, rhetorical devices, and subjective
  • interpretation to engage readers and make commentary more relatable and persuasive.
